solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: With what mill produces, is hard to thrive

parts.note: a mill grinds grain into this powder
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A miller musing that a business built on milling struggles to prosper.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the clue so the miller's product, IS and H run straight together.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish is to grow vigorously and prosper, a direct synonym of thrive.

clue.text: Road event may take place here?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wide street, often tree-lined
second, punning meaning: split as two words, it is the article plus a place where events are held

explanation.surface: A street that is about to host some event, such as a parade or a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the second meaning only works when the answer is split as A VENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad town street, so it is a kind of road; read as two words it names an event location.

clue.text: Hairy getting ship initially into UN harbour

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something done initially comes at the start, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: first letter of ship
a haven is a sheltered harbour

explanation.surface: A scruffy sailor whose vessel puts into a United Nations port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' could be adjective or slang for frightening; here it means bearded or stubbly, the definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unshaven has stubble or a beard growing, so their face is hairy.

clue.text: Employed in university post vacated by Newton

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university

indicators.note: a place vacated by someone has lost its occupant, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: Someone working at Cambridge in the professorship Isaac Newton once held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a job, but it is the verb to send; Newton is the unit N, not Isaac. SEND without N leaves SED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something employed has been put to work or made use of, which is the past participle sense.

clue.text: Very little boy trapping insect

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a son is a boy
a midge is a small biting fly

explanation.surface: A tiny lad catching a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very little' seems to describe the boy, but it is the definition. The usual spelling is SMIDGEN; this longer variant is also standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a tiny amount, so it means a very small quantity of something.

clue.text: Hostile state evacuated square

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: an evacuated building is emptied of its contents, leaving just the shell of outer letters

parts.note: outer letters of square

explanation.surface: An enemy nation clearing people out of a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a country, but it is the verb meaning to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse means having a strong dislike or opposition, close to being hostile towards something.

clue.text: English eleven with time to go out

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
XI is eleven in Roman numerals
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The England cricket or football team waiting for the moment to walk out onto the field.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'eleven' is a team in cricket and football, but here it is just the Roman numeral XI.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to leave a place, which is the same action as going out.

clue.text: Exists on old fruit

indicators.note: one thing placed on another follows it in an across answer, setting the order of the parts

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
something that exists lives

explanation.surface: Someone surviving on nothing but stale fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, A on B puts A after B.
explanation.definitionFit: Olives are the small stoned fruits of the olive tree, so they are an example of fruit.

clue.text: Medicine re-ordered with pressure for new widespread disease

indicators.note: putting things in a different sequence rearranges them, so the letters are mixed up
one thing standing for another takes its place, so a letter is swapped out

parts.note: taken as written
P is the symbol for pressure
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A drug prescribed again, this time to fight an outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the N of MEDICINE for P to get MEDICIPE, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is an outbreak of illness affecting many people at once across a community.

clue.text: Manage to go round one dilapidated historic site

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tourist succeeding in touring a crumbling ancient monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manage to go round' reads like completing a visit; Manage is RUN and it goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruin is the decayed remains of an old building, such as a castle or abbey left standing.

clue.text: What might make you choke — but not quietly

indicators.note: saying 'but not' excludes something, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: to gasp is to struggle for breath, as when choking
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A warning about something that could leave you spluttering, though not in silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choke' does double duty: it ends the definition and also supplies GASP, which loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Toxic or thick fumes in the air can make a person cough and struggle for breath.

clue.text: Too similar to sage

parts.note: like means similar to
sage as an adjective means wise

explanation.surface: Something tasting almost exactly like the herb sage.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage looks like the herb, but it is the adjective meaning wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Likewise means also or in addition, the same sense as the adverb too.

clue.text: Fresh shoe insert needs trimming to begin with

parts.note: an insole is a pad placed inside a shoe

indicators.note: what comes to begin with sits at the very start, so just the leading letters count

parts.note: first letters of needs and trimming

explanation.surface: A new shoe insole has to be cut to size before you wear it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like new, but it means cheeky; 'trimming' looks like cutting, but only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh in its informal sense means cheeky or impudent, which matches being rude and disrespectful.

clue.text: Facilitate rental agreement, knocking off pounds

indicators.note: knocking something off removes it, so a letter is struck out

parts.note: a lease is a contract to rent property
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Smoothing a tenancy deal by cutting the price.
explanation.walkthrough: Knocking off pounds sounds like a discount; it removes the L from LEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease a process is to make it simpler or smoother, the same as helping it along.

clue.text: Burn slowly and decompose after seconds

indicators.note: coming after something places it later in sequence, fixing the order of the parts

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for seconds
to moulder is to rot away

explanation.surface: Something that catches light gently and then crumbles within moments.
explanation.walkthrough: S for seconds goes in front of MOULDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoulder is to give off smoke while burning without flame, a slow, low fire.

clue.text: Wasted item's not good

indicators.note: saying something is not there excludes it, so a letter is left out

parts.note: a thing is an item
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Something thrown away because it was no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' reads as squandered, but it means emaciated; the 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wasted by illness has lost a lot of weight and looks gaunt and skinny.

clue.text: Local inhabitant innocent about beginning of troubles

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: naive means innocent or unworldly

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which alone is wanted

parts.note: first letter of troubles

explanation.surface: A local unaware that trouble is starting.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside NAIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is a person born in a particular place, so they are one of its local residents.

clue.text: Small lawsuit involving introduction of needless penalty

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: to involve something is to include it, so one piece takes in another

parts.note: a legal action is a lawsuit

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening, so just its first letter is used

parts.note: first letter of needless

explanation.surface: A minor court case that ends in a pointless fine.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside ACTION, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanction is a punishment imposed for breaking a rule or law, which is a penalty.

clue.text: Drum mostly filled with a fruit

indicators.note: something filled with another thing holds it inside, so one piece goes within
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a tom-tom is a tall drum beaten by hand
taken as written

explanation.surface: A barrel almost completely packed with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: TOMTOM loses its final M to give TOMTO, and A goes in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a tomato is a fruit, the seed-bearing part of the plant, though often treated as a vegetable.

clue.text: Violent whirlwind has ripped off flap

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so letters leave the word

parts.note: a tornado is a violent rotating storm
torn means ripped

explanation.surface: A twister tearing a loose tent flap clean away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ripped off flap' reads as the storm tearing away a flap; really the tornado has TORN taken off. Flap means a fuss, not a piece of canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap is informal for a state of agitation or fuss, and ado means needless fuss or bother.

clue.text: Seemingly only off in the middle of the day

definitions.meaning: first, jokey meaning: split into a refusal word and a word for working, it appears to say 'not on', which is all that off means

explanation.surface: A light switch that only appears to be off around lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seemingly' says the word merely looks like it means off: split as NO ON, i.e. not on.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is twelve o'clock, midday, exactly halfway through the daylight hours.

clue.text: Soldiers being silly going topless

indicators.note: losing the top of a down answer removes its first letter

parts.note: barmy is British slang for crazy or silly

explanation.surface: Troops fooling around by stripping off their shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: Barmy is everyday British slang for daft; drop its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a large organised body of soldiers, so the word stands for soldiers collectively.

clue.text: Spy undercover in Smolensk

indicators.note: something undercover inside a place is concealed within it, so the letters sit inside the word

parts.note: the letters run consecutively inside the Russian city name

explanation.surface: An agent working in secret in the Russian city of Smolensk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undercover' fits the spy story perfectly, while also signalling the concealed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a secret agent embedded long-term inside an organisation, a kind of spy.

clue.text: Arrogantly order excavation replacing centre of Dover

indicators.note: replacing the centre means swapping out the middle letter for something else

parts.note: taken as written
a mine is a dug-out excavation

explanation.surface: Someone bossily commanding digging work in the middle of the port of Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: The V at the centre of DOVER gives way to MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To domineer is to assert control over others in an overbearing, bossy way, giving commands arrogantly.

clue.text: Question tea party organiser when three characters go missing?

indicators.note: characters going missing are letters lost, so three are removed

parts.note: the Mad Hatter hosts the tea party in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Interrogating the Mad Hatter after some guests vanish from his tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' seems to mean people at the party, but it means letters: D, H and A go from the middle of MADHATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter is an issue or subject under discussion, the same as a question to be settled.

clue.text: Can tyres get shredded in race?

indicators.note: shredded things are torn into pieces, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A motor-racing worry: could the tyres disintegrate during the race?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like a motor race, but it means a line of descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Race in the sense of lineage or stock means a line of descent, which is what ancestry is.
